related_questions.snippet: Common side effects include pain at the injection site, fever, body aches and headaches. text_blocks.snippet: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that most adults receive an updated COVID-19 booster shot to stay up-to-date with the latest protections.

list.snippet: Adults 18 years of age and older who received their last primary series of COVID-19 vaccines at least 6 months ago
Adults 65 years of age and older, regardless of when they received their last primary series or booster dose
People with certain underlying medical conditions that put them at high risk for severe illness from COVID-19
Bivalent booster: Protects against both the original virus and the Omicron BA.4 and BA.5 subvariants
Updated booster: Protects against newer variants of the virus, such as XBB.1.5
Talk to your healthcare provider about getting a booster.
Visit a pharmacy or community health center that offers COVID-19 vaccines.
Check with your local health department for vaccination sites.
The CDC recommends that people who are immunocompromised or live in long-term care facilities receive a booster dose sooner after their previous vaccination.
Pregnant and breastfeeding women should consult with their healthcare provider about getting a booster.
For more information, visit the CDC website: https://www.cdc.gov/covid/vaccines/stay-up-to-date.html
